cases.name: grafana_time_projection
cases.query_origin: Grafana PostgreSQL data source macro expansion, captured from executedQueryString
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT pickup_datetime AS "time", total_amount FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime BETWEEN '2026-09-19T00:00:03.123Z' AND '2026-09-19T03:00:07.456Z' ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: A raw time projection has no bucket, so it is only safe as a whole object.

cases.name: grafana_time_epoch_projection
cases.query_origin: Grafana PostgreSQL data source macro expansion, captured from executedQueryString
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT extract(epoch from pickup_datetime) as "time", total_amount FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime BETWEEN '2026-09-19T00:00:03.123Z' AND '2026-09-19T03:00:07.456Z' ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: An epoch projection without a grouping cadence establishes no reusable buckets.

cases.name: grafana_time_group_timescaledb_between
cases.query_origin: Grafana PostgreSQL data source macro expansion, captured from executedQueryString
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime BETWEEN '2026-09-19T00:00:03.123Z' AND '2026-09-19T03:00:07.456Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: The TimescaleDB-mode $__timeGroup bucket. The inclusive BETWEEN upper reaches only the first instant of its bucket, so it normalizes to the exclusive bound on the grid; the unaligned lower rounds up.

cases.name: grafana_time_group_alias_interval_half_open
cases.query_origin: Grafana PostgreSQL data source macro expansion, captured from executedQueryString
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('120.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:03.123Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:07.456Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: $__interval resolved to two minutes; explicit $__timeFrom/$__timeTo give the half-open range that loses nothing but the partial edges.

cases.name: grafana_time_group_vanilla_epoch_floor
cases.query_origin: Grafana PostgreSQL data source macro expansion, captured from executedQueryString
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT floor(extract(epoch from pickup_datetime)/300)*300 AS "time", count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime BETWEEN '2026-09-19T00:00:03.123Z' AND '2026-09-19T03:00:07.456Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: The $__timeGroup bucket with the TimescaleDB option off: epoch seconds as a numeric, over a timestamp column with timestamp bounds.

cases.name: grafana_unix_epoch_group_alias_filter
cases.query_origin: Grafana PostgreSQL data source macro expansion, captured from executedQueryString
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT floor((pickup_epoch)/600)*600 AS "time", count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_epoch >= 1789776003 AND pickup_epoch <= 1789786807 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: An integer epoch-seconds column. The inclusive upper normalizes to the exclusive grid bound, rendered one second short of the next bucket.

cases.name: grafana_unix_epoch_group_from_to
cases.query_origin: Grafana PostgreSQL data source macro expansion, captured from executedQueryString
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT floor((pickup_epoch)/600)*600 AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_epoch >= 1789776003 AND pickup_epoch < 1789786807 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: The unaliased macro with explicit integer bounds and a half-open range.

cases.name: grafana_unix_epoch_nano_filter
cases.query_origin: Grafana PostgreSQL data source macro expansion, captured from executedQueryString
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_epoch >= 1789776003123000000 AND pickup_epoch <= 1789786807456000000
cases.rationale: A range filter with no bucket is a whole object.

cases.name: grafana_metric_column_series
cases.query_origin: Grafana PostgreSQL data source macro expansion, captured from executedQueryString
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('900.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", cab_type AS metric, count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:03.123Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:07.456Z' GROUP BY time, cab_type ORDER BY time
cases.rationale: Grafana's multi-series shape: the metric column is a group column, and rows within a bucket keep the origin's order.

cases.name: grafana_top_n_table
cases.query_origin: Grafana PostgreSQL data source macro expansion, captured from executedQueryString
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT pickup_neighborhood_name AS neighborhood, count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime BETWEEN '2026-09-19T00:00:03.123Z' AND '2026-09-19T03:00:07.456Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY trips DESC LIMIT 10
cases.rationale: LIMIT cannot be preserved across merged extents.

cases.name: time_bucket_interval_keyword
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '1 hour', pickup_datetime) AS time, avg(total_amount) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: The INTERVAL keyword form of a width.

cases.name: time_bucket_seven_day_phase
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('7 days', pickup_datetime) AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-08-01T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: TimescaleDB's grid starts on Monday 2000-01-03, four days off the Unix epoch for a 7-day width; a wrong phase would reject every bucket the origin returns.

cases.name: time_bucket_seven_hour_phase
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('7h'::interval, pickup_datetime) AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-08-01T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: A width that does not divide a day has a non-zero epoch phase on TimescaleDB's grid.

cases.name: time_bucket_typed_origin
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('1h', pickup_datetime, TIMESTAMPTZ '2000-01-01 00:20:00+00') AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: A typed timestamptz third argument is the origin.

cases.name: time_bucket_typed_offset
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('1h', pickup_datetime, '15m'::interval) AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: A typed interval third argument is the offset.

cases.name: time_bucket_untyped_third_argument
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('1h', pickup_datetime, 'Europe/Berlin') AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: An untyped string resolves to the time zone overload, whose grid follows DST.

cases.name: time_bucket_month_width
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('1 month', pickup_datetime) AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-08-01T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Calendar widths have no fixed cadence.

cases.name: time_bucket_integer_width
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket(300, pickup_epoch) AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_epoch >= 1789776000 AND pickup_epoch < 1789786800 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: The integer-time overload is not modeled.

cases.name: date_bin_zoned_origin
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT date_bin('15 minutes', pickup_datetime, TIMESTAMPTZ '2001-01-01 00:05:00+00') AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: PostgreSQL 14+ date_bin with its required origin.

cases.name: date_trunc_under_utc
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT date_trunc('hour', pickup_datetime) AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: date_trunc truncates in the session zone, which is the epoch grid only under UTC.

cases.name: date_trunc_under_local_zone
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT date_trunc('hour', pickup_datetime) AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Under Asia/Kolkata the hour grid sits at :30; the fixed phase would be wrong, so it fails closed.

cases.name: zoneless_bounds_under_utc
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19 00:00:00' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19 03:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: A zone-less literal is a UTC instant only while the session zone is UTC.

cases.name: zoneless_bounds_under_local_zone
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19 00:00:00' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19 03:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: PostgreSQL reads the literal in the session zone, so the analyzer's UTC reading would be another range.

cases.name: zoned_bounds_under_local_zone
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:03.123Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:07.456Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Zone-suffixed bounds and time_bucket's UTC grid do not depend on the session zone.

cases.name: open_ended_range
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: No upper bound: a synthetic exclusive upper is added per fetch and the newest bucket is never considered complete.

cases.name: gapfill_single_series
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket_gapfill('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' AND pickup_borough_name = 'Saltmarrow' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: start and finish are inferred from the rendered WHERE range; an empty sub-range still returns the full NULL grid.

cases.name: gapfill_locf
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket_gapfill('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, locf(count(*)) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: locf reads the value before a gap, which a sub-range cannot see.

cases.name: gapfill_interpolate
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket_gapfill('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, interpolate(avg(total_amount)) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: interpolate reads across extent edges.

cases.name: gapfill_multi_series
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket_gapfill('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, cab_type, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
cases.rationale: A sub-range emits no rows for a series absent from it, where the full query has NULL rows.

cases.name: gapfill_open_ended
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket_gapfill('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: The origin rejects this; a synthetic finish would turn its error into data.

cases.name: gapfill_explicit_start_finish
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket_gapfill('5m', pickup_datetime, '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z', '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z') AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Explicit start and finish arguments are not rewritten per extent.

cases.name: inclusive_upper_less_or_equal
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime <= '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: <= behaves as BETWEEN's upper.

cases.name: reversed_operands
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' <= pickup_datetime AND '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' > pickup_datetime GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Bounds written literal-first.

cases.name: exclusive_lower_on_raw_column
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime > '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: A strict lower bound on the raw column makes the first bucket partial.

cases.name: no_complete_bucket
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('7 days', pickup_datetime) AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:03.123Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:07.456Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Rounding inward leaves no complete bucket.

cases.name: two_lower_bounds
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T01:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Two lower bounds on the time axis are ambiguous.

cases.name: epoch_column_timestamp_bounds
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT floor((pickup_epoch)/600)*600 AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_epoch >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_epoch < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: An epoch column compared with timestamps is not the range the bucket is over.

cases.name: epoch_column_millisecond_bounds
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT floor((pickup_epoch)/600)*600 AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_epoch >= 1789776000000 AND pickup_epoch < 1789786800000 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Bounds in another epoch unit than the bucket's.

cases.name: or_across_time_axis
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' OR cab_type = 'blue' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: OR can widen the range beyond the bounds.

cases.name: not_between
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime NOT BETWEEN '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: A negated range is not a range.

cases.name: not_wrapped_bound
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE NOT (pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z') AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Negation hides the comparator's direction.

cases.name: not_equal_on_time_axis
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime <> '2026-09-19T01:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: An inequality punches a hole in a bucket.

cases.name: qualified_quoted_aliased
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('5m', t."pickup_datetime") AS "time", t.cab_type AS "Cab", count(*) FROM public.trips AS t WHERE t.pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND t."pickup_datetime" < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Qualified, quoted and aliased identifiers.

cases.name: comments
cases.expanded_sql:
/* panel 1 */ SELECT time_bucket('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, -- bucket
 count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' /* range */ GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Line and block comments are not part of the identity.

cases.name: respelled_constructs
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, max(extract(dow FROM pickup_datetime)) AS dow, max(cab_type::text) AS cab, max(passenger_count::int) AS riders, count(*) FILTER (WHERE vendor_id <> current_user) AS n, max("binary") AS b FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Constructs the parser's formatter writes in a way PostgreSQL rejects or changes are re-spelled.

cases.name: filter_and_ordered_set
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY total_amount) AS p95, count(*) FILTER (WHERE payment_type <> 'CSH') AS card FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Every aggregate is computed inside one bucket, so FILTER and ordered-set aggregates are safe.

cases.name: descending_order
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC
cases.rationale: Buckets are replayed newest first.

cases.name: continuous_aggregate_rebucketed
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('900s', bucket) AS time, cab_type AS metric, sum(trips) AS trips FROM trips_15m WHERE bucket >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND bucket < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Re-bucketing a continuous aggregate's bucket column keeps it delta-cacheable.

cases.name: continuous_aggregate_bare
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT bucket AS time, cab_type, trips FROM trips_15m WHERE bucket >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND bucket < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: No bucket function and no GROUP BY.

cases.name: cte
cases.expanded_sql: WITH recent AS (SELECT * FROM trips) SELECT time_bucket('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, count(*) FROM recent WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: A CTE can carry its own range.

cases.name: from_subquery
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, count(*) FROM (SELECT * FROM trips) AS t WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: A subquery can carry its own range.

cases.name: join
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('5m', t.pickup_datetime) AS time, count(*) FROM trips t JOIN zones z ON z.gid = t.pickup_zone_gid WHERE t.pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND t.pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: ON clauses are not inspected.

cases.name: window_function
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, avg(count(*)) OVER (ORDER BY time_bucket('5m', pickup_datetime) ROWS BETWEEN 11 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: A window frame spans buckets.

cases.name: distinct_on
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT DISTINCT ON (cab_type) time_bucket('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, cab_type FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' ORDER BY cab_type, 1
cases.rationale: DISTINCT ON picks rows across buckets.

cases.name: having
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) > 10 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: HAVING is evaluated per fetch and is kept off the delta path.

cases.name: union
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 UNION ALL SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1
cases.rationale: Compound selects.

cases.name: from_only
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, count(*) FROM ONLY trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: The parser drops ONLY, which changes the result on a hypertable.

cases.name: json_cast
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, max(payload::json ->> 'a') FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: The parser re-spells json as jsonb, another type.

cases.name: unicode_escape_string
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' AND cab_type = U&'\0062lue' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: The parser reads U&'..' as an operator expression.

cases.name: set_returning_function
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, generate_series(1, 3) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Set-returning functions are kept off the delta path.

cases.name: named_arguments
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('1 day', pickup_datetime, origin => '2000-01-01') AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: The parser does not accept named-argument notation.

cases.name: rollup
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, count(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY ROLLUP (1)
cases.rationale: The parser does not accept ROLLUP.

cases.name: ungrouped_bucket
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, total_amount FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z'
cases.rationale: A bucket that is not grouped yields raw rows.

cases.name: order_by_non_output
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY max(total_amount)
cases.rationale: An ordering the merged result cannot reproduce.

cases.name: catalog_query
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT c.relname FROM pg_catalog.pg_class c WHERE c.relkind = 'r' ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Client introspection is a whole object.

cases.name: volatile_select
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT random()
cases.rationale: A volatile result must never be replayed.

cases.name: clock_select
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT now()
cases.rationale: The clock outside a time bound is volatile.

cases.name: volatile_predicate
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' AND total_amount < random() * 100 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: A volatile predicate changes each fetch.

cases.name: clock_outside_bound
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT time_bucket('300.000s',pickup_datetime) AS "time", count(*) AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-19T00:00:00Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-19T03:00:00Z' AND dropoff_datetime < now() GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: Only a clock read that is a time bound is resolved.

cases.name: sleep
